About

A short introduction

I’m Houcine, currently working out the shape of my next academic and professional steps. English is one possible foundation; business management and international management are also on the table. I’m trying to choose a path that builds practical ability rather than relying on the title of a degree alone.

I keep coming back to a few connected interests: how people think, how decisions get made, how organisations create value, and how to distinguish a convincing idea from one that survives contact with reality. This site gives those interests a place to meet.

It is not a finished résumé or a claim to expertise. It is a public notebook: some entries will be considered essays, others will be early frameworks or experiments. I want the difference to be visible, and I want the work to improve over time.

Where I am now

At the point of choosing a direction for university and building the skills that will make that education useful. I am weighing language and communication against a more direct business route, while keeping international opportunities in view.

Questions I keep returning to

  • What makes an idea useful enough that someone will give it time, money, or attention?
  • How can a negotiation create an agreement without pretending both sides want the same thing?
  • Which parts of a business decision require human judgment, and which can be made faster with better tools?
  • How do I know when an argument is strong — and what evidence would make me revise it?

What I am trying to learn

  • Clearer English writing and communication.
  • Business fundamentals: customers, costs, cash flow, strategy, and operations.
  • Negotiation, incentives, and the practical side of working with people.
  • Research methods that separate assumptions, evidence, and conclusions.
  • Using AI as an assistant while remaining responsible for the reasoning and final result.

Direction

Long term, I want to build things, negotiate well, take responsibility, and earn the ability to lead. For now, those are directions rather than achievements. The useful question is what I can learn and demonstrate next.
